answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-weighted pulse: every agent must periodically post a small refundable bond to stay live, and each heartbeat renews its vertex in the trust graph. New identities start at the graph's cold edge, like a glacier — slow to gain weight, because reputation only accrues through verified work over time. Spinning up a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds and waiting months for each to warm up, so the attack costs far more than any fake reputation it could buy.
